cohort: 29 pregnant women with a maternal solitary kidney were compared to 60 healthy pregnant women as controls, all from a single tertiary hospital.
finding: Pregnant women with a solitary kidney are at a significantly higher risk of encountering pregnancy complications, including gestational hypertension, preeclampsia (three-fold increased risk), preterm labor (seven-fold increased risk), spontaneous abortion, earlier birth, higher serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels, and increased rates of cesarean delivery and maternal intensive care requirements.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rates were significantly higher in pregnant women with a solitary kidney compared to healthy controls (p = 0.035).
